scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: One workstation in Campus 1 -- PC11, one of the
172.16.20.x machines -- has fallen off the network entirely. From that desk
you cannot reach anything: not the machines next to it, not the usual first
stop out, nothing at all. Every other desk around it is fine, and nothing
was moved or changed at that desk, so this is not something we did: the
network has dropped PC11 on your side. Look at why exactly that one machine
is cut off and put it back on today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce the outage for PC11. The network path for 172.16.20.11 is fully operational end-to-end.

Evidence:
- Topology-wide reachability shows PC11 successfully pings same-VLAN peers (pc9/pc10) and routed subnets (e.g., 172.16.10.5). Peers also reach PC11.
- On PC11, eth0 is UP with 172.16.20.11/24 and default gateway 172.16.20.254; ARP has stable entries for peers and the gateway.
- Pings from PC11 to its gateway (172.16.20.254) and to neighbors succeed with 0% loss and sub-millisecond RTTs.
- From pc9, ARP shows PC11’s MAC reachable; pc9→pc11 pings succeed.

Mechanism: Successful ARP resolution and ICMP within VLAN20 and across the routed gateway confirm L2 switching on switch2 (ports for VLAN20) and L3 forwarding at the default gateway are normal. There is no indication of port shutdown, VLAN mismatch, or gateway reachability issues.

Localization: PC11 (switch2.eth5 access_vlan20_port6), peers on access_vlan20_port4/5, and default gateway 172.16.20.254 are all reachable.

Root cause: No network-side fault is present at this time; the reported isolation of PC11 cannot be reproduced.

Corrective fix: No configuration changes required—PC11 is currently “back on” and functioning. If the symptom recurs, check the desk NIC/cable and capture switch2 port counters/administrative state at the moment of failure, and consider enabling brief port monitoring to catch transient link flaps.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN hosts, and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly shows PC11 reaches its gateway, same-VLAN hosts, and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss.

The agent's conclusions are directly supported by the probe outputs (interface up, ARP entries, successful pings to gateway, intra-VLAN and inter-subnet hosts).
